description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, divisibility, and number systems

number_types.rational: Q = a/b where a, b are integers and b ≠ 0; terminating or repeating decimals
number_types.irrational: Cannot be expressed as fraction; non-repeating, non-terminating decimals (π, √2, e)
number_types.real: R = all rational and irrational numbers

primes.definition: Natural number > 1 with exactly two divisors: 1 and itself
primes.fundamental_theorem: Every integer > 1 is either prime or a unique product of primes
primes.sieve_of_eratosthenes: Ancient algorithm to find all primes up to a limit
primes.infinitude: Euclid proved there are infinitely many primes

rules.11: Alternating sum of digits divisible by 11

divisibility.gcd: Greatest Common Divisor; largest number dividing both
divisibility.lcm: Least Common Multiple; smallest number divisible by both
divisibility.euclidean_algorithm: GCD(a,b) = GCD(b, a mod b); repeat until remainder is 0

modular_arithmetic.definition: a ≡ b (mod n) means n divides (a - b)
modular_arithmetic.fermats_little: If p is prime and gcd(a,p)=1, then aᵖ⁻¹ ≡ 1 (mod p)

famous_theorems.goldbach: Conjecture: every even integer > 2 is the sum of two primes (unproven)
famous_theorems.riemann_hypothesis: All non-trivial zeros of zeta function have real part 1/2 (unproven)
famous_theorems.fermats_last: No three positive integers a, b, c satisfy aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ for n > 2 (proved by Wiles, 1995)
famous_theorems.four_color: Any planar map can be colored with 4 colors so no adjacent regions share colors (proved 1976)

number_bases.hexadecimal: Base 16; digits 0–9 and A–F; used in computing
